from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Counting subsets with constraints is hard.",
            "Generating functions simplify the problem.",
            "P(x) stores counts as coefficients."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Combinatorial Bottleneck", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        items = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(12)])
        items.arrange_in_grid(3, 4, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(items, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        barrier = Rectangle(color="#FF4500", width=4, height=3)
        barrier_label = Text("Complexity Barrier", color="#FF4500", font_size=20)
        barrier_group = VGroup(barrier, barrier_label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(barrier_group, "C3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(FadeIn(items), FadeIn(barrier_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Filter: Roots of Unity", [
            "Euler’s formula links algebra and geometry.",
            "Roots of unity filter modulo sums.",
            "Symmetric points on the unit circle."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Euler’s formula: e^(iθ) = cosθ + i sinθ
        euler_formula = MathTex(r"e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i \sin\theta", color="#FFCC00")
        self.place_at_grid(euler_formula, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(euler_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Unit circle visual
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        k = 6
        points = []
        labels = []
        for j in range(k):
            angle = 2 * PI * j / k
            point = Dot(point=circle.get_center() + 1.5 * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]), color="#00FFCC")
            points.append(point)
            label = Tex(f"$\\omega^{j}$", font_size=20, color="#00FFCC")
            label.next_to(point, normalize(point.get_center() - circle.get_center()), buff=0.1)
            labels.append(label)
            
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.play(*[FadeIn(p) for p in points], *[Write(l) for l in labels])
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFCC"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotation illustration
        rotation = VGroup(*points, *labels)
        self.play(Rotate(rotation, angle=PI/3, about_point=circle.get_center()))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF66CC"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Integrating Logic: The Root Extraction Technique", [
            "Combine generating functions with roots.",
            "Sum P(omega^j) to extract results.",
            "Complex lens isolates specific counts."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display polynomial P(x) in #00CED1
        p_x = MathTex("P(x) = \\sum a_n x^n", color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(p_x, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(p_x))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display extraction formula
        formula = MathTex("\\frac{1}{k} \\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} P(\\omega^j) = \\sum_{n \\equiv 0 \\pmod k} a_n", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'D3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize complex roots
        roots = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FF6347").move_to(self.grid[pos]) 
                         for pos in ['E2', 'E3', 'E4', 'E5']])
        self.play(Create(roots))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Counting Constrained Sets", ["Evaluate (1+x)^n at cube roots.", "Simplify using polar forms.", "Sum constraints extract valid configurations."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Evaluate (1+x)^n at cube roots.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        expr = MathTex(r"(1+x)^n", color=BLUE)
        root1 = MathTex(r"\omega = e^{2\pi i / 3}", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(expr, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(root1, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(expr), Write(root1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Simplify using polar forms.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        polar1 = MathTex(r"1+\omega = \sqrt{3}e^{i\pi/6}", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(polar1, 'D3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(polar1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sum constraints extract valid configurations.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        sum_form = MathTex(r"\frac{1}{3} \sum_{k=0}^2 (1+\omega^k)^n", color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_form, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_form))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Intuition", [
            "Complex numbers solve discrete counting.",
            "Algebraic evaluation replaces manual analysis.",
            "Vectors cancel to leave pure sums."
        ])
        
        # Geometry: Roots of Unity / Cancellation
        center = self.grid["C3"]
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE).move_to(center)
        roots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(center + 1.5 * RIGHT * np.cos(i * 2 * PI / 5) + 1.5 * UP * np.sin(i * 2 * PI / 5))
            for i in range(5)
        ])
        vectors = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(start=center, end=root.get_center(), color=RED, buff=0)
            for root in roots
        ])
        
        geom = VGroup(circle, roots, vectors)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(circle), FadeIn(roots))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Create(vectors))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Rotate(vectors, angle=PI/2, about_point=center), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeOut(geom))
        
        recap = Text("Efficiency: O(n) vs O(2^n)", font_size=32, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(recap, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(recap))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Generating Functions and Roots of Unity: The Magic of Complex Counting
outline.target_audience: University students majoring in Mathematics or Computer Science

sections.title: The Combinatorial Bottleneck (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the challenge: counting subsets with specific constraints (e.g., sum of elements divisible by k). Traditional methods involve tedious case analysis. Transition to the generating function: P(x) = Σ a_n x^n, where the coefficients a_n are the values we want to count.
sections.example: A squirrel collecting acorns: finding the number of ways to pick an even number of acorns from 10 distinct trees.

sections.title: The Filter: Roots of Unity (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite: Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cosθ + i sinθ. Explain the 'Roots of Unity Filter': The sum (1/k) * Σ ω^(j*n) equals 1 if k divides n, and 0 otherwise, where ω = e^(2πi/k). Visualize this on the complex plane as k symmetric points on the unit circle.
sections.example: Visualizing the roots of unity as k 'robotic arms' pointing at symmetric positions on a clock face in the complex plane.

sections.title: Integrating Logic: The Root Extraction Technique (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Combine the concepts: To find the sum of coefficients a_n where n ≡ 0 (mod k), use the identity: Sum = (1/k) * Σ P(ω^j) for j=0 to k-1. Demonstrate how evaluating the polynomial P(x) at complex points 'extracts' the desired subset information.
sections.example: A 'magic scanner' (the polynomial) that ignores irrelevant data and only highlights results divisible by k when viewed through the complex lens.

sections.title: Application: Counting Constrained Sets (3:30-4:30)
sections.content: Walkthrough a specific problem: Calculate the sum of binomial coefficients (n choose r) where r is a multiple of 3. Substitute ω = e^(2πi/3) into (1+x)^n. Show how (1+ω)^n + (1+ω^2)^n simplifies using the polar form of complex numbers.
sections.example: A computer system filtering packets: The system counts valid configurations by evaluating the 'Generating Function' at the three cube roots of unity.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Reiterate that complex numbers turn discrete counting problems into algebraic evaluation problems. Conclude with the visual of rotating and canceling vectors in the complex plane to isolate the count.
sections.example: Final snapshot: The complex plane showing the cancellation of unwanted 'counts' (vectors) to leave only the desired sum.
